land.text: the Kedun garrison, 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province'

predecessors.note: Yelü Dashi, a prince of the Liao, fled the Jin conquest with a band of officials to the Liao garrison of Kedun in 1124; the Liao fell in 1125 ('Emperor Tianzuo was captured by the Jin dynasty in 1125'). Only the garrison and its steppe pass to the new state; the Liao proper went to the Jin.

successors.note: 'The Mongols fully conquered the former territories of the Qara-Khitai in 1220' (Qara Khitai page); Kuchlug, who had usurped the throne in 1211, was killed in 1218 (Kuchlug page). Part of the Syr Darya and Transoxiana had gone to the Khwarezmid Empire in 1210-1216 (see the ledger).

capitals.name: Kedun (Zhenzhou)
capitals.note: 'the military garrison of Kedun (Zhenzhou)'; the Yelü Dashi page: 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province'. The site is not located by the pages: the coordinates are a rough point in Bulgan Province, not a surveyed position.

capitals.name: Emil base (near Tacheng)
capitals.note: 'On 13 March 1130 he headed west'; 'he established a new base on the Emil River'. Coordinates of Tacheng from the gazetteer, the nearest listed place to the Emil valley.

capitals.name: Balasagun (Quz Ordu)
capitals.note: 'He made Balasaghun his new capital' (1134). Infobox 'Capital: Balasagun' with no years; the page has no later seat, so it is held to Kuchlug's death in 1218.

rulers.name: Dezong (Yelü Dashi)
rulers.note: Gurkhan; ruler table 1124-1144, but the text and the Yelü Dashi page have him die in 1143 ('two years after Qatwan'). Proclaimed Gurkhan in 1132 (Yelü Dashi page).

rulers.name: Empress Gantian (Xiao Tabuyan)
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: Regent for her son; table 1144-1150, text 1143-1150.

rulers.name: Empress Dowager Chengtian (Yelü Pusuwan)
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: Regent; table 1164-1178, text 1164-1177; killed in a coup by Xiao Wolila in 1178.

rulers.name: Yelü Zhilugu
rulers.note: Captured by Kuchlug while hunting in 1211 and left as a nominal ruler; the page has him die about 1213.

rulers.name: Kuchlug
rulers.note: The Naiman prince who usurped the throne in 1211; 'a usurper, not a formal Qara Khitai emperor' in the table; captured and killed in 1218.

correction.text: the Kedun garrison, 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1124-1129 (Cliopatria's row starts in 1126; the infobox has 'Yelü Dashi proclaims himself king: 1124'). 'In 1124, Yelü Dashi fled northwest and established his headquarter at the military garrison of Kedun' on the Orkhon with about 20,000 troops. The gazetteer has no Kedun; the Orkhon Valley region (73,000 km2) is the nearest named land and is generous for a garrison and its followers.

correction.text: the Kedun garrison, 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province'

keyframe_review.note: 1126-1138, 376,585 km2 (88.7-101.0 E, 42.6-47.9 N: the Mongolian Gobi and Gobi-Altai and the Hami side of Xinjiang, no Orkhon cells). No page puts the Qara Khitai there: Kedun on the Orkhon 1124-1129, the Emil base in 1130, Balasagun and Zhetysu from 1134. The infobox area 1,000,000 km2 (c. 1130) is for the later realm, 2.7 times this shape. Replaced by the new keyframes _1124, _1130, _1134 and _1137.

correction.text: a town and first base by the Emil river, trimmed to the Kimek-Kipchak edge and to the Eastern shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1130-1133: the Emil base. 'On 13 March 1130 he headed west with less than 20,000 men'; 'he established a new base on the Emil River'; the ruler of Qocho 'became his ally or vassal' (vassal_start in the ledger); the attack on Kashgar in the summer of 1131 failed. The base is a town and its pasture: a 120 km radius around Tacheng is a generous reading. Review fix: the disk is trimmed to the Kimek edge. Cliopatria's Kimek-Kipchak shape (1094-1138) covers 58 of its 151 cells, about a third, and the Kimek dossier has no loss there; the Qara Khitai page is silent on who held the Emil land before 1130, so no gain from the Kimek row is claimed and the base keeps 92 cells (about 23,000 km2; one further cell lies in the Eastern 1126 shape and is left to it until 1134). The capital point (Tacheng) stays inside it.

union.text: Balasagun, Zhetysu and the Tian Shan: the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern 1126 shape (Kucha added), 1,860 cells, the same cells as the eastern-kara-khanids loss of 1134
a town and first base by the Emil river, trimmed to the Kimek-Kipchak edge

correction.text: Balasagun, Zhetysu and the Tian Shan (the non-Tarim part of the Eastern shape), with the Emil base

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1134-1136: Balasagun taken and made the capital ('In 1134 he conquered the Karakhanid city of Balasaghun'; 'He made Balasaghun his new capital'). 'Under the empire's direct rule was the region around their capital, Balasagun.' The Emil base is kept as the north-eastern end, trimmed to the Kimek edge. Review fix: the region is the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern Kara-Khanid 1126 shape (1,860 cells, about 470,000 km2: Zhetysu, the Tian Shan interior, the Alay and the Pamir edge), the cells the eastern-kara-khanids dossier loses in 1134. The first version drew Semirechye only: 129 of its 1,435 cells (north of Lake Balkhash, in the Kimek row's land) were never Eastern, and 554 Eastern cells (about 140,000 km2) were drawn by no dossier in 1134-1138 and by this one only from 1139 (reviewer ia-01-g).

union.text: Balasagun, Zhetysu and the Tian Shan: the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern 1126 shape (Kucha added), 1,860 cells, the same cells as the eastern-kara-khanids loss of 1134
a town and first base by the Emil river, trimmed to the Kimek-Kipchak edge

correction.text: Balasagun, Zhetysu and the Tian Shan, the Emil base, and the Fergana valley and Tashkent oasis

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1137-1138: the Fergana valley and Tashkent added after the May 1137 victory over the Western Karakhanids at Khujand ('He consolidated power in the Ferghana valley and Tashkent for several years'). The cells of 1134 stay (the non-Tarim part of the Eastern shape, 1,860 cells); the Emil base is trimmed to the Kimek edge.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1139 shape without Qocho, Hami and the Tarim rump (vassals) and with the Fergana valley and Tashkent oasis

keyframe_review.note: 1139-1146, 1,803,946 km2 by polygon (1.57 M km2 by cells). Cliopatria's shape is the whole Eastern Kara-Khanid shape (Balasagun, the Tarim, 776,000 km2), Qocho (584,000 km2) and 212,000 km2 of Dzungaria and Hami. The pages make Qocho and the Kara-Khanids vassals ('Within a year, he had established himself as suzerain of Qocho'; 'Despite losing to the Qara Khitai, the Karakhanid dynasty remained in power as their vassals') and give direct rule only to 'the region around their capital, Balasagun'. Corrected to the direct land: the shape without Qocho, Hami and the Tarim rump, plus Fergana and Tashkent. Hami (Yizhou) is Qocho's in the qocho-kingdom dossier, whose corrected shape adds Hami (120 km) from the 876 seizure of Yizhou, and the Qara Khitai page gives Hami only as the end of the southern boundary ('from Balkh to Khotan to Hami'); 109 cells (about 27,000 km2) were drawn by both dossiers before this fix (reviewer ia-01-g). That is 0.75 M km2 by cells (2969 cells) against the infobox 1,000,000 km2 (c. 1130, ratio 0.75), where Cliopatria's 1.57 M km2 is 1.6 times the infobox. The vassals come back through the vassal events. The Dzungaria part (the 1139 gain, now 636 cells without Hami and the Emil base) has only the page's 'After 1137 ... conquer Kashgar, Khotan, and Beshbalik' behind it.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1147 shape without Qocho, Hami, the Tarim rump, the Khwarezmid Dynasty cells of 1146 (Khwarazm), and the Samarkand-Bukhara vassal land

keyframe_review.note: 1147-1151, 2,568,396 km2 by polygon (2.22 M km2 by cells): the 1139 shape plus the whole Western Karakhanid shape (1,278 cells), 292 cells of the middle Syr Darya taken from the Kimek-Kipchak row and Kyzylkum and Khwarazm-edge cells out to 60.5 E. The Qatwan page makes Samarkand's khanate and Khwarazm vassals in 1141-1142, not annexed land, and the Qara Khitai page gives 'Its western border was defined by the Amu Darya'. Corrected to the direct land: the Cliopatria shape without Qocho, Hami, the Tarim rump, the Samarkand-Bukhara part of the Western shape and the Khwarezmid Dynasty cells. Review fix: the 975 cells that this shape gains in 1147 from Cliopatria's Khwarezmid Dynasty 1146 shape (the Kyzylkum, the lower Syr Darya and Khwarazm's edge, 60.5-68.5 E, 40.1-46.2 N, about 245,000 km2; 73 of them in Khwarazm proper) were kept as direct land with no event and no counterpart (reviewer ia-01-g). No page gives the Qara Khitai direct rule there: Khwarazm is a vassal from 1141-1142 and 'Its western border was defined by the Amu Darya', so they are left to the khwarezmid-dynasty row (me-09) and the vassal event of 1142; Cliopatria's step is a disagreement with the pages, not a gain. That leaves 0.83 M km2 by cells (3264 cells); the infobox gives 1,500,000 km2 only for c. 1210. Balkh and Andkhud (vassal land 1165-1198 per the page) are not in the Cliopatria shape; see the ledger.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1152 shape without Qocho, Hami, the Tarim rump, the Khwarezmid Dynasty cells of 1146 (Khwarazm), and the Samarkand-Bukhara vassal land

keyframe_review.note: 1152-1201, 2,512,509 km2: the 1147 shape without 218 cells (55,000 km2, Pamirs, 62-76 E, 37-41 N) that Cliopatria hands to its Lohara row; unverified: page silent. Same correction as 1147. In the corrected direct shape the step removes 48 of the 218 cells (the others lie in the Tarim rump or the Samarkand-Bukhara vassal land) and adds 32 others.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1202 shape without Qocho, Hami, the Tarim rump, the Khwarezmid Dynasty cells of 1146 (Khwarazm), and the Samarkand-Bukhara vassal land

keyframe_review.note: 1202-1205: 4,000 km2 of change on the Pamir edge; unverified: page silent. The Qara Khitai page has the 1198 loss of Balkh to the Ghurids and the 1204 Kashgar-Khotan rebellions, neither of which moves the Cliopatria shape. Same correction as 1147.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1206 shape without Qocho, Hami, the Tarim rump, the Khwarezmid Dynasty cells of 1146 (Khwarazm), and the Samarkand-Bukhara vassal land

keyframe_review.note: 1206-1209: 1,000 km2 of change in the east; unverified: page silent. Qocho rebels in 1209 (ledger). Same correction as 1147.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1210 shape without Qocho, Hami, the Tarim rump (the Eastern Khanate's vassal land to 1211, held by the Kashgar rebels to 1214) and the Samarkand-Bukhara land; holds 1210-1213

keyframe_review.note: 1210-1215, 2,059,424 km2 by polygon: the western 383,000 km2 (60.5-68.5 E: Bukhara, Khwarazm's edge, the Kyzylkum and the lower Syr Darya) go to Cliopatria's Khwarezmid Empire row. The Kara-Khanid page has the Khwarezm-Shah take Samarkand in 1210 after the Qara Khitai retreated, and Qocho left the Qara Khitai in 1209 for the Mongols (Qocho page 'In 1209, the Kingdom of Qocho became a vassal of the Mongol Empire'). Corrected: the Cliopatria shape without Qocho (a Mongol vassal from 1209), Hami (Qocho's) and the Samarkand-Bukhara vassal land. Review fix: the Tarim rump is out of the direct shape for 1210-1213. The Eastern dossier holds it as a Qara Khitai vassal to 1211, so 1,122 cells (about 283,000 km2) were drawn by both dossiers in 1210-1211 (reviewer ia-01-g), and the Kara-Khanid page has the Kashgar rebels hold Kashgar after the killing of 1211 and surrender to Kuchlug only in 1214; this shape holds 1210-1213 and the new keyframe _1214 adds the rump. 0.79 M km2 by cells (3115 cells) against the infobox 1,500,000 km2 (c. 1210, ratio 0.53); with the Tarim rump (0.32 M km2) and Qocho with Hami (0.62 M km2), which the infobox may count as vassals, about 1.7 M km2. Cliopatria's 2.06 M km2 (1.79 M by cells) is 1.4 times the infobox; all within a factor of two.

correction.text: the 1210 shape as corrected, with the Tarim rump (Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu, Kucha) added: Kuchlug's realm after the Kashgar rebels' surrender

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1214-1215: the 1210 shape (as corrected) with the Tarim rump added. 'The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211' (the prince 'was killed in Kashgar by the rebels in 1211'), and 'the rebels in Kashgar surrendered to Kuchlug, who had usurped the Kara-Khitai throne' in 1214 (Kara-Khanid page). The page does not say who ruled the other Tarim cities (Khotan, Yarkand, Aksu, Kucha) in 1212-1213 or when they came under Kuchlug; the whole rump is read as passing with Kashgar (confidence 2), and is kept whole (1,249 cells) as the successor land of the eastern-kara-khanids dossier, a little more than the 1,122 cells of Cliopatria's 1210 shape. 1.10 M km2 by cells (4364 cells) against the infobox 1,500,000 km2 (c. 1210, ratio 0.73). The reviewer asked for the split at 1212; the page puts the rump's change of hands in 1214, so the split is there.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1216 shape without Qocho (a Mongol vassal from 1209) and Hami, with the Tarim rump kept whole; held to 1220

keyframe_review.note: 1216-1219 (held to 1220, the end of the state): 304,000 km2 more (66.6-78.5 E, 37.1-45.9 N: Samarkand, Fergana and Tashkent) go to the Khwarezmid Empire row; unverified: no page opened dates a Khwarazmian conquest of Fergana or Tashkent in 1216 (the Kuchlug page has 'In 1216, Genghis Khan dispatched his general Jebe to pursue Kuchlug'). Corrected for Qocho, which was a Mongol vassal from 1209, and for Hami (Qocho's); the Tarim rump stays in (Kuchlug's realm, 0.91 M km2 by cells in all, 3581 cells). The pursuit and the end are in the ledger.

region.text: the Kedun garrison, 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province'

ledger.note: 1124: Yelü Dashi, fleeing the Jin conquest of the Liao, sets up his headquarters at the garrison of Kedun on the Orkhon. 'In 1124, Yelü Dashi fled northwest and established his headquarter at the military garrison of Kedun' with about 20,000 troops; infobox 'Yelü Dashi proclaims himself king: 1124'. The Liao itself fell in 1125. The region is the Orkhon Valley of the gazetteer.

region.text: Qocho as the qocho-kingdom dossier draws it: Cliopatria's 1126 shape without Gansu, Kucha and Aksu, plus Hami (Yizhou), the Uyghur kingdom whose ruler 'became his ally or vassal'

ledger.note: 1130: the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho submits to Dashi. 'Within a year, he had established himself as suzerain of Qocho' (the Yelü Dashi page: about 1130 the ruler 'became his ally or vassal'). The Qocho page has 1128 in its text and 1132 in its infobox ('Vassal of the Western Liao: 1132-1209'); the Qara Khitai page repeats Qocho among the states vassalised in 1134. Kept at 1130 in the review (ia-01-g): the Qara Khitai page has Dashi 'within a year' of heading west in March 1130 suzerain of Qocho, and the Yelü Dashi page has it about 1130, while 1128 (the Qocho text) falls before Dashi's move west and 1132 is the Qocho infobox's. qocho-kingdom /ledger/6 has 1128; ia-01-f should move it to 1130 and record the conflict in its note. The region is the Qocho dossier's own corrected shape, which also holds Hami.

1130: Dashi leads his people west. 'On 13 March 1130 he headed west with less than 20,000 men' and 'established a new base on the Emil River' (the Qara Khitai page: 'settled a town and his first base by the Emil river'). Destination: the Emil base, near Tacheng; no month for the founding of the base.

region.text: Balasagun, Zhetysu and the Tian Shan: the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern 1126 shape (Kucha added), 1,860 cells, the same cells as the eastern-kara-khanids loss of 1134

ledger.note: 1134: Dashi takes Balasagun, the Kara-Khanid capital of the north. 'In 1134 he conquered the Karakhanid city of Balasaghun'; the page: 'Under the empire's direct rule was the region around their capital, Balasagun'. The city is the page's; the extent is the reading (confidence 2): the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern 1126 shape, 1,860 cells or about 470,000 km2 (Zhetysu, the Tian Shan interior, the Alay and the Pamir edge), the cells the eastern-kara-khanids dossier loses in 1134. The first version gained Zhetysu only and left 554 of those cells with no gain (reviewer ia-01-g).
1134: Balasagun becomes the capital. 'He made Balasaghun his new capital.'

region.text: the Karluks of Qayaliq and Almaliq

ledger.note: 1134: the Karluks of the Almaliq region become Dashi's vassals. 'In 1134 he conquered the Karakhanid city of Balasaghun, leading to vassalization of the Kankalis, Karluks, Kyrgyz, and Qocho'; the page also has Dashi strengthening 'his forces to eventually expand his authority in Qayaliq and Almaliq regions'. The Kangli and the Yenisei Kyrgyz are named by the page without land and are not drawn.

region.text: the Fergana valley and Tashkent oasis, the part of the Western Karakhanid shape that Dashi 'consolidated' after May 1137

ledger.note: 1137: Dashi defeats the Western Karakhanids at Khujand and takes the Fergana valley and Tashkent. 'In May 1137 he defeated a Western Karakhanid ruler at Khujand'; 'He consolidated power in the Ferghana valley and Tashkent for several years.' The page gives the battle and the land, not the date of the transfer.

region.text: Dzungaria: the 636 cells (about 161,000 km2) of the Cliopatria 1139 shape that are neither the Eastern shape, Qocho with Hami, nor the Emil base

ledger.note: 1139: Dzungaria is in Qara Khitai hands. 'After 1137 ... conquer Kashgar, Khotan, and Beshbalik' (Qara Khitai page); the Yelü Dashi page: Dashi 'gained control over what is now Xinjiang'. Neither gives a year; 1139 is Cliopatria's step. The land is neither Qocho (a vassal) nor the Tarim rump (the Kara-Khanids), so no state is named. Review fix: Hami is no longer in this gain; the qocho-kingdom dossier's corrected shape holds it, and the Qara Khitai page gives it only as the end of the southern boundary ('from Balkh to Khotan to Hami'), which fits a vassal's land. The first version gained 'Dzungaria and Hami' (212,000 km2 on Cliopatria's polygon) and drew Hami twice (reviewer ia-01-g).

region.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern Kara-Khanid shape: Kashgar, Khotan, Aksu, Kucha

ledger.note: 1141: the Kara-Khanids of Kashgar are Qara Khitai vassals. The Kara-Khanid infobox: 'Qara Khitai vassal (1141-1212)'; the Qara Khitai page has the Khitans conquer Kashgar, Khotan and Beshbalik 'after 1137' and Dashi attack Kashgar in 1131. The Eastern khans remain at Kashgar until 1211.

region.text: Samarkand, Bukhara and the rest of the Western Karakhanid shape, a vassal after Qatwan (1141)

ledger.note: 1141: Dashi wins at Qatwan and the Kara-Khanids of Samarkand become his vassals. 'The battle took place on the Qatwan steppe, north of Samarkand, on 9 September 1141'; Dashi 'appointed Mahmud's brother Ibrahim as ruler of Samarkand' and 'let the Burhan family keep ruling Bukhara'; the Kara-Khanid page: 'the Karakhanid dynasty remained in power as their vassals'. The Seljuk dossier should end its own vassalage of the same khanate in 1141.

region.text: Khwarazm, tributary from 1142

ledger.note: 1142: Khwarazm is made to pay tribute. The Qara Khitai page's chronology for 1142: Khwarazm is forced to pay 30,000 dinars in annual tribute after Dashi's general Erbuz raids it (the Qatwan page: 'Yelü sent Erbuz to Khwarazm to pillage the province' and Atsiz agrees to the tribute). Khwarazm is Cliopatria's Khwarezmid Dynasty, then Khwarezmid Empire.

region.text: 292 cells on the middle Syr Darya (44.0-46.7 N, 61.9-72.4 E)

ledger.note: 1147: the middle Syr Darya steppe is in Qara Khitai hands. Cliopatria's step (292 cells taken from its Kimek-Kipchak row); the page gives only the western border 'defined by the Amu Darya' and no date for the Syr Darya steppe. The Kimek-Kipchak dossier records the matching loss at 1147.

region.text: 218 cells in the Pamirs

ledger.note: 1152: 55,000 km2 of the Pamirs pass to the Lohara row. Cliopatria's step (218 cells at 62-76 E, 37-41 N); the page is silent.

region.text: Balkh and Andkhud

ledger.counterpart: Balkh vassal (the page does not name the holder)
ledger.note: 1165: Balkh and Andkhud come under Qara Khitai rule through a vassal. 'In 1165, the Qara Khitai participated in Mas'ud Tabghach Khan's invasion of Balkh and Andkhud' (as the page's chronology reads, the towns were under Oghuz control); Balkh then stayed under Qara Khitai rule until 1198, and in 1198 Muhammad of Ghor 'seized Balkh from the vassal of the Qara Khitai'. The holder is therefore a vassal, drawn as the lighter tint, not direct land (reviewer ia-01-g); the page does not name him. The year is the page's, the region is the page's two towns, the vassal status is read from the 1198 sentence (confidence 2). Not in the Cliopatria shape.

region.text: Balkh and Andkhud

ledger.counterpart: Balkh vassal (the page does not name the holder)
ledger.note: 1198: Muhammad of Ghor seizes Balkh from the vassal. 'In 1198, Muhammad of Ghor, one of the Ghurid rulers, seized Balkh from the vassal of the Qara Khitai'; the Qara Khitai invade Ghurid lands at Kurzuban and lose 12,000 men. The conqueror is the Ghurid dynasty (ghurid-dynasty, sa-04, should carry the gain with this vassal as counterpart). The page names only Balkh for 1198; Andkhud is the researcher's reading (confidence 2, reviewer ia-01-g).

region.text: Kashgar and Khotan

ledger.note: 1204: the Qara Khitai put down rebellions at Kashgar and Khotan. In 1204 the Qara Khitai 'put down a rebellion in Khotan and Kashgar' (the Kara-Khanid page: 'a rebellion of the Eastern Kara-Khanid in Kashgar was suppressed by the Kara-Khitai').

region.text: Kashgar and Khotan

ledger.note: 1204: the rebellions are suppressed and the Kara-Khanids stay vassals.

region.text: Qocho as the qocho-kingdom dossier draws it: Cliopatria's 1126 shape without Gansu, Kucha and Aksu, plus Hami (Yizhou), the Uyghur kingdom whose ruler 'became his ally or vassal'

ledger.note: 1209: Qocho rebels and goes over to the Mongols. The page's chronology for 1209: Qocho rebels, the Qara Khitai commissioner is killed, and the Uyghur ruler Barchuq submits to Genghis Khan. The Qocho page: 'In 1209, the Kingdom of Qocho became a vassal of the Mongol Empire.'

region.text: Samarkand, Bukhara and the rest of the Western Karakhanid shape, a vassal after Qatwan (1141)

ledger.note: 1210: the Khwarezm-Shah takes Samarkand and defeats the Qara Khitai. 'In 1210, the Khwarezm-Shah took Samarkand after the Qara Khitai retreated'; Muhammad had 'formed an alliance with the Western Karakhanid ruler Uthman ibn Ibrahim'. The vassalage of the Western Khanate to the Qara Khitai ends here.

region.text: Khwarazm

ledger.note: 1210: Khwarazm throws off the tribute. 'The Khwarezm-Shah then defeated the Qara Khitai near Talas' (the page does not date the battle; the Qara Khitai page: 'Khwarazm returned to paying tribute ... in 1209-10').

region.text: the 144 cells (about 36,000 km2) of the direct shape that Cliopatria hands to its Khwarezmid Empire row in 1210

ledger.note: 1210: the western edge of the direct land passes to Khwarazm. The Kara-Khanid page has Muhammad take Samarkand in 1210 and divide the Qara Khitai empire with Kuchlug; Cliopatria gives the Khwarezmid Empire 383,000 km2 at 60.5-68.5 E (Bukhara, the Kyzylkum, the lower Syr Darya). Review fix: most of those cells are no longer in this dossier's direct shape (the Samarkand-Bukhara land is the Western Khanate's vassal land, vassal_end 1210; the Khwarezmid Dynasty cells and Khwarazm itself were never taken as direct land), so the loss is the 144 cells, about 36,000 km2, that were. The page names Samarkand, not the Kyzylkum.

1211: the Naiman Kuchlug seizes the throne. 'in 1211, while Yelü Zhilugu was out hunting, he was ambushed and captured by Kuchlug'; 'Many historians consider Kuchlug's usurpation of the throne in 1211 to be the end of the Qara Khitai.' Kept as one state under a usurper (the ruler table: 'not a formal Qara Khitai emperor').

region.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern Kara-Khanid shape: Kashgar, Khotan, Aksu, Kucha

ledger.note: 1211: the Eastern Kara-Khanid prince is killed at Kashgar by rebels and the Eastern Khanate ends. 'The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211'; the page does not say who held Kashgar next. The Kashgar rebels who killed the prince hold Kashgar until they surrender to Kuchlug in 1214 (the gain of 1214 below).

region.text: the Karluks of Qayaliq and Almaliq

ledger.note: 1211: the Karluk Arslan Khan surrenders to Genghis Khan. The Qara Khitai page has the Karluk Arslan Khan surrender to Genghis Khan in 1211.

region.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern Kara-Khanid shape: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Kucha

ledger.note: 1214: the Tarim rump passes to Kuchlug's Qara Khitai. 'The rebels in Kashgar surrendered to Kuchlug, who had usurped the Kara-Khitai throne' (Kara-Khanid page), after they killed the Eastern prince at Kashgar in 1211. The page names Kashgar only and does not say who held Khotan, Yarkand, Aksu and Kucha in 1212-1213 or when they submitted; the rump is read as passing with Kashgar (confidence 2). Mirrors the dissolve of eastern-kara-khanids (1211), whose successor land this is; the rebels are a counterpart without a dossier. The Kuchlug page dates nothing for Kashgar or Khotan.

region.text: the whole Qara Khitai realm as it stood in 1216

ledger.note: 1216: Genghis Khan sends Jebe against Kuchlug. 'In 1216, Genghis Khan dispatched his general Jebe to pursue Kuchlug.' The page names the pursuit, not the ground fought over; the whole realm is the zone.

region.text: the 785 cells (about 199,000 km2) of the direct shape at Samarkand, Fergana and Tashkent that Cliopatria hands to its Khwarezmid Empire row in 1216

ledger.note: 1216: Samarkand, Fergana and Tashkent pass to Khwarazm. Cliopatria's step (304,000 km2 to its Khwarezmid Empire row, of which 785 cells, about 199,000 km2, are direct land in this dossier; the rest is Qocho's or the Western vassal land); no page opened dates it. The Kara-Khanid page has Samarkand in Khwarazmian hands from 1210.

region.text: the whole Qara Khitai realm as it stood in 1216

ledger.note: 1220: the Mongols finish the conquest. 'The Mongols fully conquered the former territories of the Qara-Khitai in 1220.' Kuchlug had been captured and killed in 1218.

region.text: the last Cliopatria shape, held to 1220

ledger.note: 1220: the Qara Khitai are absorbed into the Mongol Empire. Infobox 'All former territories fully absorbed into Mongol Empire: 1220'.

wars.name: Qara Khitai conquest of the Eastern Kara-Khanid lands
wars.outcome: Dashi is repelled at Kashgar in the summer of 1131, takes Balasagun in 1134 and, after 1137, Kashgar, Khotan and Beshbalik; the Kara-Khanids of Kashgar stay on as vassals.
wars.note: 'In the summer of 1131 he attacked Kashgar' (Yelü Dashi page).

wars.name: Qara Khitai conquest of the Fergana valley (Khujand)

zones.text: the Fergana valley and Tashkent oasis, the part of the Western Karakhanid shape that Dashi 'consolidated' after May 1137

wars.outcome: Dashi defeats the Western Karakhanids at Khujand in May 1137 and consolidates the Fergana valley and Tashkent.

wars.name: Qara Khitai attack on the Jin
wars.outcome: 'A disastrous attack on the Jin leads Dashi to give up recapturing northern China.' No land changed hands.
wars.note: Later contacts with the Jin (a 1156 meeting of armies at Kedun, the 1146 execution of the Jin envoy) are diplomatic.

wars.name: Battle of Qatwan
wars.outcome: Qara Khitai victory on 9 September 1141 north of Samarkand: 'a decisive defeat for the Seljuks'; Samarkand's khanate and Khwarazm become vassals.
wars.note: No land changed hands; the suzerain of Transoxiana changes from the Seljuks to the Qara Khitai. Cliopatria hands the land to Kara-Khitans in 1147.

wars.name: Qara Khitai-Khwarazm tribute wars
wars.outcome: Khwarazm pays 30,000 dinars a year from 1142; the Qara Khitai attack it in 1172 over neglected tribute and enthrone Tekish on 11 December 1172; tribute resumes in 1209-10; Muhammad II defeats the Qara Khitai near Talas and takes Samarkand in 1210.
wars.note: The Kara-Khanid page has Muhammad II 'defeated the Qara Khitai near Talas' without a year.

wars.name: Qara Khitai-Ghurid war at Balkh
wars.outcome: Muhammad of Ghor seizes Balkh; the Qara Khitai invade at Kurzuban and lose 12,000 men.
wars.note: Balkh and Andkhud had been Qara Khitai since 1165; in 1204 the Qara Khitai sent 10,000 or 40,000 men to help Muhammad II of Khwarazm after a Ghurid defeat.

wars.name: Kashgar and Khotan rebellions
wars.outcome: The rebellions at Kashgar and Khotan are put down.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Qara Khitai
wars.outcome: Kuchlug, defeated by the Mongols in 1208, takes refuge with the Qara Khitai, usurps the throne in 1211, is pursued by Jebe from 1216 and is captured and killed in 1218; 'The Mongols fully conquered the former territories of the Qara-Khitai in 1220.'
wars.note: The Kara-Khanid page has Muhammad II and Kuchlug 'apparently agreed to divide the Qara Khitai empire between them' in 1210.

certainty.note: Steppe, mountain and oasis frontiers throughout, no treaty line: the page gives the western border as the Amu Darya, the southern 'from Balkh to Khotan to Hami', the northern as the Yenisei Kyrgyz north of Lake Balkhash until 1175, and the eastern as 'hard to define'.

sources.title: Qara Khitai
sources.note: Infobox (1124, 1,000,000 km2 c. 1130, 1,500,000 km2 c. 1210, 1220), chronology, vassals, ruler table, borders; read twice with different questions.

sources.title: Yelü Dashi
sources.note: Flight to Kedun, 13 March 1130, Emil base, 1131 Kashgar, 1132 Gurkhan, 1134 Balasagun, May 1137 Khujand, 1143 death.

sources.title: Battle of Qatwan
sources.note: 9 September 1141, the settlement at Samarkand and Bukhara, Khwarazm tribute 1142.

sources.title: Qocho
sources.note: 1128 and 1132 dates for the Qocho vassalage, 1209 Mongol vassalage.

sources.title: Kara-Khanid Khanate
sources.note: Qara Khitai vassalage 1141-1212, 1204, 1210 Samarkand and Talas, 1211 end of the Eastern Khanate.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: the first shape (1126-1138, 356,000 km2 by cells) is wrong: it lies on the Gobi, not at Kedun on the Orkhon or at the Emil; four new keyframes replace it. From 1139 the Cliopatria shapes draw Qocho and the Tarim rump (the Eastern Kara-Khanids) as Qara Khitai land, and from 1147 the whole Western Karakhanid shape; the pages make all three vassals (Qocho from about 1130, the Eastern Khanate and Samarkand from 1141), so the verdicts take them out of the direct shape and the ledger carries them as vassals with the shapes of the eastern-kara-khanids and western-karakhanid-khanate dossiers. Overlaps for the compile stage: the same Transoxiana cells are Great Seljuk Empire to 1146 in Cliopatria and the Western Khanate's vassal land in the dossier; the Qocho row ends 1138 in Cliopatria but the Qocho dossier (another batch) ends it in 1128 as a Qara Khitai vassal.
End: the infobox and the page say 1220 ('fully conquered'); Kuchlug was killed in 1218 and many historians end the Qara Khitai in 1211. The dossier ends in 1220, with the 1211 usurpation as a rename.
Areas: infobox 1,000,000 km2 c. 1130 and 1,500,000 km2 c. 1210. Cliopatria 376,585 km2 for 1126-1138 (ratio 0.38 to the infobox's c. 1130 figure, wrong shape), 1.80 M km2 for 1139 and 2.06 M km2 for 1210 (ratio 1.4 to the c. 1210 figure). After the review fix the corrected direct shapes are 0.75 M km2 (1139), 0.83 M km2 (1147-1209), 0.79 M km2 (1210-1213), 1.10 M km2 (1214-1215) and 0.91 M km2 (1216-1220) by cells (253 km2 a cell), all within a factor of two of the infobox (1.0 M c. 1130, 1.5 M c. 1210), which may count the vassals.
Unsettled: (1) the date of Qocho's submission (1128 in the Qocho text, 1132 in its infobox, about 1130 in the Yelü Dashi page, 1134 in the Qara Khitai chronology; kept at 1130 here and ia-01-f should move qocho-kingdom's 1128 to 1130); (2) the Kara-Khanid page has the Eastern khans at Kashgar to 1211, the Qara Khitai page has the Khitans 'conquer Kashgar, Khotan, and Beshbalik' after 1137; (3) steps without a page behind them (confidence 1): 1139 Dzungaria, 1147 middle Syr Darya, 1152 Pamirs, 1216 Samarkand-Fergana-Tashkent to Khwarazm; (4) the Battle of Talas is dated by no page opened; (5) the page budget (5) was exceeded by one, to take the Kara-Khanid page for 1141, 1204, 1210 and 1211.
Missing: the northern frontier retreat of 1175 (Yenisei Kyrgyz and the Naiman 'until 1175', undated in effect), the Kangli, Kyrgyz and Naiman as vassals (no land named), the Jin frontier, Western Xia, the Karluk and Kangli dossiers. Counterparts needing dossiers: Naiman, Kangli, Karluks of Almaliq, Kakuyids (Qatwan belligerent).
Review fixes (ia-01-g, 2026-10-19): (1) the 1134 gain, the 1134 and 1137 keyframes now hold the whole non-Tarim part of the Eastern 1126 shape (1,860 cells), matching the eastern-kara-khanids loss; (2) the Khwarezmid Dynasty 1146 cells (975 cells, 972 of them kept) and the Khwarezm region are out of the direct shape of 1147-1209: no page gives direct Qara Khitai rule there, and Cliopatria's 1147 step is treated as a disagreement; (3) the Tarim rump is out of the direct shape for 1210-1213 and enters in 1214 (new keyframe _1214, gain from the Kashgar rebels) because the Kara-Khanid page has the Kashgar rebels surrender to Kuchlug in 1214; the reviewer asked for 1212; (4) Hami is out of the direct shape (the Qocho dossier holds it) and the Qocho vassal events use the Qocho dossier's own corrected region; (5) the Emil base is trimmed to the Kimek edge (58 of 151 cells lay in the Kimek row) instead of claiming a gain from it; (6) Balkh and Andkhud are a vassal pair 1165-1198, not a gain and a loss; (7) the Qocho vassal year stays 1130. Direct-shape overlaps with the Eastern, Qocho (with Hami) and Kimek dossiers are now zero in every year (cell counts with gazetteer.resolve). Pages re-read: Qara Khitai (three queries), Kara-Khanid Khanate (two), Kuchlug (one); Malik-Shah I, Ibrahim Tamghach Khan and Cumans were opened for the other two dossiers.
